text:
sasha: quick sync — I'm proposing we add a 'retirement queue' pattern for deprecated service surfaces. idea: instead of immediate removals, put calls onto a retire queue + shim that returns a soft-deprecation header and routes to fallback. allows staged client upgrades and gives us a clear paydown window.
ryan: can you sketch the guarantees? is this just traffic mirroring -> redirect, or do we still serve payloads?
sasha: plan sketch: 1) requests to deprecated endpoints get enqueued for async processing (no error for client). 2) a shim responds 200 with X-Deprecation: true + small payload indicating grace period. 3) behind the queue we run a compatibility processor that updates telemetry, logs failing payloads, and optionally replays to new service for validation.
anna: sounds promising. two quick concerns: SLO impact for callers during deprecation, and increased ops surface for queue processing.
mike: for SLOs we should set a hard limit: if queue depth > 90th pct threshold we flip to hard forward (fail fast) or route to dedicated fallback. otherwise risk unbounded latency.
sasha: agreed — default behavior is immediate soft response (O(10ms)) while enqueuing happens async. queue processing is best-effort for migration/insights. only on explicit opt-in do we rely on queue for correctness.
elaine: what about auth and idempotency? some endpoints are non-idempotent. we can't just async-process writes and pretend they happened.
ryan: for non-idempotent writes we'd set a policy: either 1) require client opt-in (they accept async semantics), or 2) perform synchronous proxy to new service during grace window. retirement queue only for read-ish or idempotent operations.
anna: we should keep the contract for deprecation transparent: telemetry + a header X-Deprecated-Until: <ts> so clients can surface it. also add a warning metric for clients hitting deprecated paths.
sasha: agreed on header + warning metric. rollout stages I propose: alpha (internal clients only, metrics + alerts), beta (external clients with soft-response header), gamma (start automated client outreach + small throttles), delta (hard cut overrides after grace period).
mike: implementation notes: prefer using existing async-worker infra (task-queue service) instead of a new queue. add a lightweight shim service that owns header injection + enqueue logic. this keeps surface small.
elaine: what's ownership of the shim? which team will support? shims historically get neglected.
sasha: ownership proposal: platform infra to own shim lifecycle; product/domain teams opt-in per endpoint and maintain the compatibility processor that consumes the queue for their domain. infra owns the routing and observability.
ryan: can we add a small schema to the queue payload so processors can validate and decide replay strategy? e.g. {path, method, body_hash, idempotency_key, client_version} — schemified so we can evolve safely.
sasha: yes. we should include a versioned envelope. example: ```{"v":1,"path":"/v1/foo","method":"POST","body_hash":"...","meta":{...}}```
anna: risk notes: people bypassing header checks and relying on soft responses is possible. we need a detector rule: if a client gets X-Deprecated-Until but still shows high error budget dependence on that endpoint, create a pager.
mike: and cost note: queue storage + processing could be non-trivial for very chatty endpoints. suggest we cap per-endpoint retention to 7 days and sample for high-volume paths.
sasha: agree to sampling and retention caps. also add an eval job: after 2 weeks we replay sampled queued messages to new endpoint and compare diffs to catch regressions.
elaine: action items?
sasha: 1) I'll write a short RFC with ops/playbook + header schema + rollouts. 2) Mike to spike shim prototype using task-queue infra (1 week). 3) Ryan and Anna to identify top 5 candidate endpoints for pilot. 4) Infra (elaine) to draft ownership & alerting runbook.
ryan: +1 to timeline. can we add an experiment id header to correlate replays? X-Retire-Exp: <id>
anna: please also include required logs/metrics: deprecations.count, deprecations.by-client, queue.depth.by-endpoint, replay.diff.rate.
mike: noted. prototype will emit those.
stilly-bot: auto: created RFC draft workspace: https://rfc.redwood.local/r/retirement-queue-1714456789
sasha: thanks. I'll post the RFC link here once initial draft is ready (ETA Tue). if anyone objects to the ownership split (infra shim + domain processors), call it out now.
elaine: fine from infra side but need SLA for shim critical bits. we'll propose 99.9% shim availability and an emergency bypass toggle.
anna: sounds reasonable. no objections from me.
ryan: no objections. excited to see the RFC.
sasha: closing thread for now — will circulate RFC and set a short sync after prototype. :thumbsup:
